about: TFR AI rules (round 1018): amended rules that review Forge's AI decisions and take priority. Rules run in this order. 'enabled' lists the adventure difficulties a rule runs at (Easy, Normal, Hard, Insane) plus Other for any game that is not an adventure duel (deck tester, benches). params.shadow=true makes a rule log what it would change ('<id> (shadow)') and change nothing: a rule earns the right to act from evidence. Edit and restart the game to switch a rule; no build needed. Every change a rule makes logs [TFR-AiRule]. The proof is res/ai/tfr-puzzles (TfrAiPuzzleTest); the merge protocol is in CORE_ENGINE_CHANGES.md.

rules.retireWhen: P1 and P2 pass with the rules off at off, lite and max (the puzzle test says RETIRE?): upstream weighs mandatory enter-the-battlefield drawbacks (our draft PR). Then delete the rule and its AiController line.

Round 1019: Flat Monte Carlo replaced the heuristic's attack with no attack on 10 turns in a row (audit g021, a 20-turn stall), on near-identical rollouts: its position score values the creatures kept home over the damage. The rule keeps the heuristic's attack unless the defender has a combat trigger or the swing back could be lethal. cuts: to-nothing (default) or any; belowSamples: only cuts on fewer samples per line (0 = any). Retire when P3b attacks at lite and max with the rules off (the puzzle test says RETIRE?): upstream stops cutting that attack (our draft PR in notes/r1019/upstream-pr). Then delete the rule and its AiController line.

Shadow since round 1018: Forge took every lethal we built (P3 at off, lite and max), and the rule's one fire in the 112-game bench lost (a block trigger killed the attacker; it now stays out when the defender has a combat trigger). Switch shadow off only when log reviews show '(shadow)' lines where the all-out attack would really have won; delete it if two releases of log reviews show none.

Round 1021: on the eldrazi_scion vs crocodile stall boards Forge declares no attack for 30+ turns: each token fails AiAttackController.shouldAttack (one blocker kills it), and the all-out level needs an attritional kill and a life-ratio lead the token side never has; nothing in between sends the surplus and keeps chump blockers home. The rule sends the surplus when its damage past the best blocks, minus lifelink (paid lifelink like Stonefare Crocodile's included), kills within 'rounds' turns at that rate, the opponent's all-out swing back into what stays home leaves the AI at 'minLifeAfter' or more, and that swing back costs no more than the chip. onlyWhenNoAttack: only when Forge declared no attack. Retire when P6 attacks at off, lite and max with the rules off (the puzzle test says RETIRE?).

Round 1025 (round 1023's study F5): Forge's pump AI judges each pump alone, so on the opponent's turn the infect deck spent Groundswell and then Primal Bellow on its 0/4 wall to kill a 2/2, and lost the poison kill they made next turn. The rule holds a pump on a blocker (no lifelink or trample involved, stack empty) when the AI's next attack kills with it kept and not with it spent, against every way the opponent's untapped creatures can block. Retire when P15 passes with the rules off at off, lite and max (the puzzle test says RETIRE?).
